entries.name: meridian.v1.AccountAttributes.error_account
entries.empty: false unless a deployment admin marked the account
entries.intent: says whether the account is the firm's error account (W9.13; step 5's Q30)
entries.meaning: true: a booking may allocate to it without the instruction naming it, every allocation carrying its reason and ErrorCause and raising an alert (W11.27, W11.34); unmarking is recorded, and past allocations keep their flag
entries.not_meaning: a FINRA Rule 4515 approval, or any regulatory status

entries.name: meridian.v1.AccountAttributes.allocation_account
entries.empty: false unless a deployment admin marked the account
entries.intent: says whether the account is an allocation account a block order is proposed in (W9.13, W11.1)
entries.meaning: true: it has no statement to reconcile against and should be flat once booked; a non-zero balance after booking holds the booking (W11.28)
entries.not_meaning: an account a client or fund owns

entries.name: meridian.v1.AccountAttributes.base_cash_instrument_id
entries.empty: empty while no base currency is set, and while the instrument store has not resolved its code
entries.intent: names the cash instrument of the account's base currency (W9.13, W12.2; ruling 316)
entries.meaning: the platform's ID of the base currency's cash instrument, which the book resolves from base_currency_code when the base is set and keeps, each resolution its own record; an account whose base was set before v26 carries it once the book holds the resolution. What the analytics component values the account in
entries.not_meaning: an attribute a person or a plugin sets, or a conversion: the book converts nothing

entries.name: meridian.v1.SetAccountAttributeRequest.error_account
entries.empty: unset unless this is the attribute
entries.intent: marks or unmarks the account as the firm's error account (W9.13)
entries.meaning: a deployment admin's, from the dashboard or dashboard__set_account_attribute, with its reason; each change its own record, unmarking never refused

entries.name: meridian.v1.SetAccountAttributeRequest.allocation_account
entries.empty: unset unless this is the attribute
entries.intent: marks or unmarks the account as an allocation account (W9.13)
entries.meaning: a deployment admin's, with its reason, each change its own record

entries.name: meridian.v1.ProposeOrderRequest.block_member_order_ids
entries.empty: empty unless the oms proposes a block order
entries.intent: names the member orders a block order merges (W11.1; step 5's link 2)
entries.meaning: each a released order of one instrument and side, compared through the replacement; the block's quantity is the sum of their idle quantities, and it is released on creation in the allocation account
entries.not_meaning: a split child's parent, or orders a firm's order represents

entries.name: meridian.v1.ProposeOrderRequest.net_member_order_ids
entries.empty: empty unless the oms proposes a net order
entries.intent: names the member orders a net order nets (W11.1; approved 2026-10-14)
entries.meaning: members of both sides, each a released FX order of one pair and one value date in no other live block or net; the net is released on creation in the allocation account, its quantity signed buys minus sells, its side the larger's. A member not released or in another live block or net is refused REFUSAL_REASON_ORDER_STATE; one of another pair or value date, or a net of one side, INVALID_ARGUMENT naming net_member_order_ids[i]; a net naming block members too, INVALID_ARGUMENT naming both
entries.not_meaning: a block's members; cross-currency netting, which is deferred

entries.name: meridian.v1.ProposeOrderRequest.value_date
entries.empty: empty is spot: the pair's spot date at release, by the date read, so two empty value dates compare equal only on one trade date
entries.intent: says the date an FX order settles on (W11.1)
entries.meaning: ISO 8601 (FIX's SettlDate, 64), as portfolio states it
entries.not_meaning: the trade date, or a settlement date the book works out

entries.name: meridian.v1.Fee.capitalised
entries.empty: false: the fee is not in a lot's cost
entries.intent: says whether a fee on an allocation enters the cost of the lot it opens (W11.27; the order-path plan's v24 item 4)
entries.meaning: the oms's choice by its policy; a capitalised fee enters the lot's cost on a buy; every fee stays its own cash line either way, so cash is unchanged, and on a sale a reader nets proceeds from the flags
entries.not_meaning: a default core sets: core sets none (26 CFR 1.1012-1(h)(1))

entries.name: meridian.v1.Booking.booking_id
entries.intent: identifies the booking
entries.meaning: minted by the book, a ULID behind its prefix, never reused (decisions/035, point 7); the reference the street echoes back
entries.not_meaning: an allocation's identifier, or FIX's AllocID as a venue keeps it

entries.name: meridian.v1.Booking.order_id
entries.intent: names the order the booking books, a block order included
entries.meaning: the order's `ORD-` ID; a child's executions are booked as its parent's
entries.not_meaning: a member order of a block, which each allocation names by its account

entries.name: meridian.v1.Booking.execution_ids
entries.intent: names the executions the booking books (W11.27)
entries.meaning: an explicit list on one order, sharing instrument, side, trade date and settlement date, as FIX's AllocationInstruction (J) requires of NoExecs; any subset of the unbooked
entries.not_meaning: every execution on the order: a late fill stays visibly unbooked

entries.name: meridian.v1.Booking.allocations
entries.intent: carries the booking's allocations, one per account
entries.meaning: summing exactly to the executions booked in quantity, gross and each fee kind, the residual on a named allocation (step 5's Q29)
entries.not_meaning: the allocation instruction, which is the order's

allowed.meaning: not said; never answered
booked, its allocations tying out, not yet handed off or closed
executed does not equal allocated -- a bust, a correction, a late fill or a later fee since booking, or a failed hand-off -- held with the reason, its alert raised (W11.28)
handed off to operations, which owns each allocation's post-trade life
a client's booking the firm does not settle, closed, its error-account allocations handed off
cancelled by the oms before the hand-off, so the executions may be booked again

entries.intent: says where the booking stands (decisions/035 as amended at v24)

entries.not_meaning: the order's state, which booking leaves unchanged but for a block's member order

entries.name: meridian.v1.BookOrderRequest.execution_ids
entries.intent: names the executions to book (W11.27)

entries.name: meridian.v1.HandOffBookingRequest.booking_id

entries.name: meridian.v1.Allocation.net_amount

the allocation's account is not marked an error account

open_meridian is no longer written, each window closed at the resolution and still resolvable; open_meridian_local, the deployment-only scheme, keeps a resolved LCL- ID for life and never leaves the deployment (the one-ID spec's requirements 1, 2 and 13)

the schemes the first templates match on are spelled as the platform builds them: share_class_figi, composite_figi, sec_series and sec_class beside figi, and ticker, a ticker carrying its venue as an ISO 10383 MIC in source, or the venue's VEN- ID where it has no MIC (ruled 2026-10-14)

the FIGI specification's three levels: share_class_figi identifies a security, one per security across its listings, and keys its INS- record; composite_figi (per country) and figi (per exchange) are listing identifiers, kept paired with their venue or country, resolved to the share class before matching, never a reason to merge two records; the composite identifies a security that has no share-class FIGI (ruled 2026-10-14)

agency_pool, an open scheme, names an agency pool by the agency's pool number with the agency in source (FNMA, FHLMC, GNMA); a debt record matches on figi and agency_pool, and cusip and isin stay deployment-side, never sent to the platform and in v29 mapped to no FIGI (rulings 677, 976)

four schemes name market participants and a security for trade reports (715; names approved 2026-10-26): mpid, FINRA's and MSRB's four-character market participant identifier, on a legal entity, a party and a venue; clearing_number, a clearing firm's number, on its legal entity; branch_sequence, a branch office's number on a party, its MPID in source; finra_symbol, FINRA's symbol for a security on an instrument record, deployment-side; each dated (decisions/034)

actual/364 (1950 = 17; CDM ACT/364)

actual days over 365

business days over 252

simple interest
compounded, periods_per_year times a year
continuously compounded

entries.name: meridian.v1.InterfaceDeclaration.loopback_port

entries.name: meridian.v1.SettingColumn.name

entries.not_meaning: what a person reads, which label is

entries.name: meridian.v1.SettingColumn.description
entries.intent: explains the column
entries.meaning: words shown beside its heading

entries.name: meridian.v1.SettingColumn.choices

entries.name: meridian.v1.RegisterReply.roles
entries.empty: empty for a plugin admitted with no topics

entries.not_meaning: the rows delivered, which its read scope also cuts

entries.name: meridian.v1.RegisterReply.refusal_reason

entries.name: meridian.v1.HeartbeatRequest.healthy

entries.meaning: words for a person; diagnostic, nothing branches on it

entries.name: meridian.v1.HeartbeatRequest.figures

entries.name: meridian.v1.Refusal.reason

allowed.meaning: no reason beyond the status
beside FAILED_PRECONDITION: the operation named an external account nobody has linked (W2, W6.4); nothing recorded, and once a link is made the next statement records it
a command other than a finding sent with no user -- a person, or from v21 a service account: an opening balance, handling, a resolution or an attribute is a user's act
a justified act sent without its reason or explanation
a second opening balance while one stands (W9.1)
a break, figures or an entry for an account with no opening balance
an entry moving a position effective on or before the opening balance's date
an opening position whose lots do not sum to its quantity, or an entry leaving a position's open lots so
a command the break's state does not allow
a reversal of an opening balance while a later entry moving the account's positions stands
an idempotency key the account's book holds for a different command: nothing applied
beside ABORTED: an entry missing a field the book requires (W9.1, W9.7); nothing applied, and each missing field named in fields by its path
the instrument store refusing one record of a completion at the dashboard: an identifier another record carries; per record, never a plugin's
a record changed since the version a completion or a merge named: read it again; per record, never a plugin's
beside UNAVAILABLE, to be tried again: the book could not check a command because the instrument store did not answer in time; nothing recorded
beside FAILED_PRECONDITION: a deletion of a unit whose last record was received inside the hold over the instance; nothing recorded, and the unit is kept

beside FAILED_PRECONDITION: a link naming an existing account the deployment admin has not granted the plugin's instance; nothing linked; from v22 also an ems's venue account mapping naming such an account (W11.22)
beside ABORTED: a release whose allocation instruction does not sum to the ordered quantity (W11.6; principle 1); nothing changed
beside ABORTED: a release of an order whose approval required stands unapproved (W11.6)
beside ABORTED: a release while a check's block stands without an override (W11.6)

beside ABORTED: a placement, a claim or a change by other than the claimant of a claimed order (W11.3, W11.7 to W11.9), and from v23 an accept onto it (W11.23); a cancel by anyone who may write the account is admitted past a claim, and so is a connectivity plugin's report of a cancel it sent under a stop

beside ABORTED: a command the order's or the placement's state does not allow, by the transition table (decisions/035): a placement or a child order under an order not released, a quantity change that is not the proposer's or an alignment, an acknowledgement of does not tie out, a use of an expired locate
beside ABORTED: a new record reusing an identifier already in use (W11.1)

beside ABORTED: a placement naming a connectivity plugin not linked to the placing ems, or not made available to the user the command acts for (W11.8), refused and recorded, an entry heard by the ems and compliance; or an ems's venue account mapping at a connectivity plugin not linked to it (W11.22)
beside ABORTED: a link of a connectivity plugin already linked to another ems (W11.21): each is linked to exactly one

beside ABORTED: an accept of venue-originated fills whose quantity, added to what the order has filled already, is past its ordered quantity (W11.23): the trader accepts to a new order instead, or portfolio upsizes first; nothing changed

beside ABORTED: an accept or a DK of an execution not unmatched -- answered already -- or of one a bust or a correction supersedes, by the transition table's e3 to e6 (W11.23, W11.24); nothing changed
beside ABORTED: an accept of fills of more than one account, instrument, side, connectivity plugin or trade date, or of a fill whose side is the order's opposite (W11.23); nothing changed
beside ABORTED: a booking or a correction whose allocations do not tie out exactly to the executions booked, in quantity, gross and each fee kind (W11.27, W11.29); nothing changed
beside ABORTED: a booking or a correction allocating to an account neither the order's allocation instruction names nor marked an error account (W11.27, W11.29); nothing changed

beside ABORTED: a proposal, or an accept of venue-originated fills, naming an instrument whose record is provisional, a local record, while the deployment's setting allows_local_record_orders is off (W11's invariant, W11.1, W11.23); nothing changed, a fill staying unmatched. FIX's OrdRejReason (103) 1, Unknown symbol

beside ABORTED: a placement, or an accept of fills to a new order, made through a delegation or by a service account on a connectivity instance that is not demo while the deployment's agent_orders_demo_only is on (W11.8, W11.23, W11.38); recorded, as the connectivity refusal is, a fill staying unmatched

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.ReceiveRequest.subjects
entries.empty: none: no conflated row is delivered
entries.intent: names the subjects a plugin wants of the conflated rows
entries.meaning: entity IDs; the sidecar delivers only the conflated rows, and from v19 the unconflated ones, about them
entries.not_meaning: rows to hear, which rows names

changes.what: narrows the unconflated rows too: the lake's trades (W4.3)

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.SubscribeRequest.subscription_id
entries.intent: names a subscription so the plugin can drop it and route what it hears (amended 2026-10-30)
entries.meaning: the plugin's own name for it, 1 to 64 characters, unique among its open subscriptions, as FIX's MDReqID (262) is the requester's; the same id and selector again is answered as the first, another selector under an open id refused ALREADY_EXISTS
entries.not_meaning: an identifier the platform minted, or one any other plugin sees

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.SubscribeRequest.row
entries.intent: names the one row a subscription hears (amended 2026-10-30)
entries.meaning: a row by its matrix name, as DeliveryMeta.row names it; a row no role the plugin holds hears is refused, PERMISSION_DENIED, naming it

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.SubscribeRequest.subjects
entries.empty: none: a lake row is about none, so nothing is heard of it; a book row's every account in the read scope
entries.intent: narrows a subscription to what a page shows (amended 2026-10-30)
entries.meaning: entity IDs: a lake row's subjects, as ReceiveRequest names them; a book row's accounts, within the read scope
entries.not_meaning: rows, which row names; an account outside the read scope, which is never heard

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.SubscribeRequest.series_keys
entries.empty: none: rows keyed by a series are heard only with all_series
entries.intent: narrows a lake row's subscription to named series (amended 2026-10-30)
entries.meaning: the series' keys, as ListQuotesRequest.series_keys names them, each row keyed by one heard with the subjects named

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.SubscribeRequest.all_series
entries.empty: false: rows keyed by a series are heard only where series_keys names them
entries.intent: subscribes to a chain (amended 2026-10-30)
entries.meaning: true: rows keyed by any series of the subjects are heard beside their own, narrowed by the window

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.SubscribeRequest.expiration_from
entries.intent: narrows a chain subscription by expiration, inclusive (amended 2026-10-30)
entries.meaning: a plain date; set only with all_series, or refused naming it; the sidecar holds the window to the series the lake's listing holds expiring in it, and to those listed later (SeriesRecorded)

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.SubscribeRequest.expiration_to
entries.intent: narrows a chain subscription by expiration, inclusive (amended 2026-10-30)
entries.meaning: a plain date, on or after expiration_from; set only with all_series, or refused naming expiration_from

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.SubscribeRequest.fields
entries.empty: none: every field the plugin may read
entries.intent: narrows what a subscription delivers to what a page shows (amended 2026-10-30)
entries.meaning: dictionary entries of the row's message, as the reads name them, intersected with the plugin's entitled fields when the subscription opens and again on EntitlementsChanged; the envelope always; an entry of another message is refused naming fields
entries.not_meaning: an entitlement: a field asked and not entitled is left unset

entries.name: SidecarSubscribe.limit
entries.empty: not a field: the bound on a plugin's subscriptions
entries.intent: bounds what one sidecar matches for its plugin (amended 2026-10-30)
entries.meaning: at most 256 open at once; one more is refused RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED naming subscription_id; identical selectors within a plugin are one subscription in the SDK
entries.not_meaning: a bound on pages or readers, which the SDK's views share

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.UnsubscribeRequest.subscription_id
entries.intent: names the subscription dropped (amended 2026-10-30)
entries.meaning: an open subscription's id; nothing more is queued for it once answered; an id not open is answered as dropped

entries.name: meridian.v1.AlgorithmDeclaration.algorithm_id

entries.not_meaning: a version of the plugin, or a person

entries.name: meridian.v1.AlgorithmDeclaration.description
entries.intent: says what the algorithm is, for a person reading the plugin's page
entries.meaning: plain text
entries.not_meaning: an instruction to anyone who reads it

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetDeclaration.calendar_id

entries.name: meridian.v1.DateBasis.rule

entries.name: meridian.v1.DateRuleRef.kind

a market's settlement-date rule, for a country and an asset class
a currency pair's spot-date rule, its tenor-date rule on it

entries.name: meridian.v1.DateRuleRef.subject
entries.intent: names what the rule is for

entries.name: meridian.v1.DateRuleRef.version
entries.intent: names the rule's version
entries.meaning: assigned by the platform; a date before a version is answered by the one before

entries.name: meridian.v1.CalendarRef.calendar_id
entries.intent: names a calendar
entries.meaning: `CAL-` and the platform's ID, never reused
entries.not_meaning: a currency code or an FpML business centre

entries.name: meridian.v1.CalendarRef.version
entries.intent: names the calendar's version
entries.meaning: monotonic, assigned by the platform, starting at 1

entries.name: meridian.v1.CallerClaims.algorithm_id

entries.intent: carries the algorithm identifier a service account's call named
entries.meaning: kept in the assertion the dashboard made for the call, so every command it makes carries it and none can name another; the sidecar checks it against the version's algorithms and stamps it on the envelope
entries.not_meaning: anything the plugin may change after the call is admitted

entries.name: meridian.v1.CallerClaims.connectivity_instance_ids

entries.intent: carries the connectivity plugin instances the user may route through for the calling ems

entries.name: meridian.v1.CallAsServiceAccountRequest.algorithm_id
entries.intent: names the algorithm the autonomous work runs
entries.meaning: one of the identifiers the version declares; checked and stamped by the sidecar on every command the act sends, and copied by the book to each entry's ServiceAccountActor; one not declared is refused INVALID_ARGUMENT naming algorithm_id

entries.name: meridian.v1.AccountScopeDelivery.connectivity_link

entries.not_meaning: accounts of its own: a connectivity plugin links none

entries.name: meridian.v1.AccountScopeDelivery.connectivity_links
entries.empty: empty except for an ems with connectivity plugins linked

entries.name: meridian.v1.AccountScopeDelivery.venue_account_map

entries.name: meridian.v1.ConnectivityLink.connectivity_instance_id

entries.meaning: an instance holding connectivity

entries.name: meridian.v1.ConnectivityLink.available

entries.meaning: true while available to link

entries.name: meridian.v1.ConnectivityLink.ems_instance_id

entries.not_meaning: every ems that may read it

entries.name: meridian.v1.ConnectivityLink.users
entries.empty: empty: nobody may route through it
entries.intent: says who may route through it

entries.name: meridian.v1.ConnectivityUser.subject

entries.name: meridian.v1.ConnectivityUser.service_account_id

entries.name: meridian.v1.ConnectivityUser.user_group_id

entries.meaning: the group, whose persons may route

entries.name: meridian.v1.VenueAccountMap.ems_instance_id
entries.intent: names the ems whose map it is
entries.meaning: the ems that sets the venue's account field at its connectivity plugins

entries.name: meridian.v1.VenueAccountMap.mappings
entries.intent: lists the ems's mappings
entries.meaning: each account's code at one connectivity plugin; what the sidecar stamps a venue fact's account by

entries.name: meridian.v1.VenueAccountMapping.connectivity_instance_id
entries.intent: names the connectivity plugin the code is at
entries.meaning: one linked to the ems

entries.name: meridian.v1.VenueAccountMapping.venue_account_code
entries.intent: carries the code the account trades under
entries.meaning: once per plugin

entries.name: meridian.v1.VenueAccountMapping.account_id
entries.intent: names the book account
entries.meaning: an account the deployment admin granted the ems's instance (W6.30)

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.AcknowledgeAlertParams.acting_for

entries.meaning: the assertion the plugin was handed for them, the same bytes, never altered; the sidecar admits it only in a session at write, when the person may write the account it names or the record it names is in their write access, and stamps them on it (W4.9)
entries.not_meaning: the plugin's own identity, which the sidecar knows

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.RaiseAlertParams.acting_for

entries.intent: names the person RaiseAlert is sent for
entries.meaning: the assertion the plugin was handed for them, the same bytes, never altered; set, the sidecar admits it only in a session at write, when the person may write the account or the record it names, and stamps them on it (W4.9)

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.OfferTemplateFieldsParams.acting_for

entries.intent: names the person OfferTemplateFields is sent for
entries.meaning: the assertion the plugin was handed for them, the same bytes, never altered; set, the sidecar admits it only in a session at write, when the person may write the account or the record it names, and stamps them on it (W4.9)
entries.not_meaning: the plugin's own identity, which the sidecar knows

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.Delivery.booking_updated
entries.empty: unset unless the delivery is a booking that changed
entries.intent: delivers a booking that changed (W11.30)
entries.meaning: the booking's whole new state with its entry, within the plugin's read scope
entries.not_meaning: an execution or an order, each its own arm

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.Delivery.alert_changed
entries.empty: unset unless the delivery is an alert raised, acknowledged or cleared
entries.intent: delivers an alert that changed (W11.35)
entries.meaning: the alert's whole new state, within the plugin's read scope

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.Delivery.replace_merged_instrument
entries.empty: unset unless the delivery is an instrument replaced
entries.intent: delivers an instrument replaced (W3.8), sequenced reference data (approved 2026-10-14)
entries.meaning: the replaced record, the record it became, why and its sequence, heard by every role whatever its scope and caught up by ListReplacements after the last sequence seen (W3.22)
entries.not_meaning: a record of the book, caught up by watermark

entries.name: meridian.v1.CallerClaims.demo_connectivity_instance_ids
entries.empty: empty in an assertion for any plugin but an ems, and where no connection the user may route through is demo
entries.intent: names those of connectivity_instance_ids that are demo (W4.9, W11.8)
entries.meaning: each instance whose environment setting, core's record, is sandbox or paper and whose venue catalogue reports the same, computed by the dashboard at admission
entries.not_meaning: a plugin's word: neither key is the plugin's to change at runtime

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.AnswerPriceBatchParams.acting_for
entries.empty: unset: a pricing plugin answers a batch as itself
entries.intent: names the person AnswerPriceBatch is sent for
entries.meaning: the assertion the plugin was handed for them, the same bytes, never altered; a batch's answer is the plugin's own act, so it is sent unset
entries.not_meaning: the plugin's own identity, which the sidecar knows

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.ReportEventGroupParams.acting_for
entries.empty: unset: a data plugin reports its venue's grouping as itself
entries.intent: names the person ReportEventGroup is sent for
entries.meaning: the assertion the plugin was handed for them, the same bytes, never altered; a venue's statement is the plugin's own report, so it is sent unset
entries.not_meaning: the plugin's own identity, which the sidecar knows

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.Delivery.price_batch
entries.empty: unset unless the delivery is a batch routed to this pricing instance
entries.intent: delivers a batch to price (W12.3)
entries.meaning: a batch for this instance alone, caught up by ListPriceBatches after a loss
entries.not_meaning: a job: a pricing plugin never sees the job or its accounts

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.Delivery.job_finished
entries.empty: unset unless the delivery is a job this instance ran finishing
entries.intent: tells the client a job answered later has finished (W12.4)
entries.meaning: the job's ID and answer hash, for this instance alone, caught up by ListFinishedJobs after a loss

entries.name: meridian.plugin.v1.Delivery.event_group_changed
entries.empty: unset unless the delivery is an event group's new version
entries.intent: delivers an event group's new version (W3.30)
entries.meaning: the group's whole new version, unscoped reference data, caught up by ListEventGroups after a sequence
entries.not_meaning: an outcome, which the lake delivers

entries.name: meridian.v1.HeartbeatRequest.model_tokens
entries.empty: empty for a plugin calling no model
entries.intent: reports the model tokens the plugin used since it started (W4.5; item 191)
entries.meaning: per endpoint, person or service account, and client; each heartbeat replaces the last, at most 64
entries.not_meaning: a prompt, an answer or a cost

entries.name: meridian.v1.ModelTokenCount.endpoint
entries.intent: names the model endpoint
entries.meaning: its host and model as the plugin names it

entries.name: meridian.v1.ModelTokenCount.subject
entries.empty: empty for the plugin's own work
entries.intent: names the person or service account the tokens were used for
entries.meaning: as the assertion named them
entries.not_meaning: an agent's identity, which client_name gives

entries.name: meridian.v1.ModelTokenCount.client_name
entries.empty: empty where no delegation was used
entries.intent: names the client of the delegation the work went through
entries.meaning: as the claims named it

entries.name: meridian.v1.ModelTokenCount.input_tokens
entries.intent: counts the tokens sent to the model
entries.meaning: since the plugin started

entries.name: meridian.v1.ModelTokenCount.output_tokens
entries.intent: counts the tokens the model answered
entries.meaning: since the plugin started

entries.name: meridian.v1.PluginDeclaration.pricing_models
entries.empty: empty from a version not holding pricing; a v26 version's metadata is read as before
entries.intent: declares the model ids and versions a pricing plugin answers batches for (W12.3)
entries.meaning: 1 to 32 on a version holding pricing, each model id and version once; refused on a version not holding pricing. A deployment admin's routing naming the instance is refused FAILED_PRECONDITION naming implementation unless its launched version lists the model id (W12.6)
entries.not_meaning: a route: the deployment admin routes each model id, and one never routed reads built-in

entries.name: meridian.v1.PricingModelDeclaration.model_id
entries.intent: names a model the version answers
entries.meaning: a model id the analytics component serves, such as quoted_price or binary_event
entries.not_meaning: an implementation, or the plugin's instance

entries.name: meridian.v1.PricingModelDeclaration.model_version
entries.intent: names the version of the model the version answers
entries.meaning: 1 or more; each model id and version is immutable once published, and an improvement is a new version a deployment admin routes

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetDeclaration.declared_delay_ns
entries.intent: says how far behind real time the vendor serves the dataset (W10.1)
entries.meaning: the delay the vendor serves it at; its staleness and its edge age are judged against the delay plus the ceiling. One dataset per timeliness: a vendor serving real-time and delayed data declares two
entries.not_meaning: the stale ceiling, which the data plugin admin's dataset_thresholds setting holds; a delay the plugin adds

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetDeclaration.price_source_class

allowed.meaning: not stated, as in every catalogue before the amendment
prices of trades done: a venue's last, its close or its settlement
prices someone stands ready to deal at: a venue's or a dealer's executable bid and ask, and the mid between them
an aggregate of several contributors' prices by the vendor's stated method, as Pyth's aggregate of its publishers is
a pricing service's or a model's evaluation, not a price dealt or offered, as an evaluated bond price or a vendor's model price is

entries.intent: says what class of source a dataset's prices come from (W10.1; amended 2026-10-31, ruling 906)
entries.meaning: one class for the dataset, beside its vendor, its aggregator and its terms' underlying source; each price keeps its real kind -- bid, mid, ask, close, last -- and the class says what stands behind it: Pyth's is a mid of class composite, an evaluated bond price a bid, mid and ask of class evaluated; shown on the Data sources page and answered by dashboard__list_datasets
entries.not_meaning: a price kind, of which none is added; a quality state; an order a default read takes, which the deployment's source priority sets (W10.2)

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.terms_version
entries.intent: names the version of the platform's standard terms filled in
entries.meaning: in a catalogue's default, the version the vendor filled in; in the deployment's licence, the version the deployment admin accepted
entries.not_meaning: the vendor's own terms' version, or a contract version

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.access_basis

allowed.meaning: not stated
licensed: the meters apply
open: free, and conditions may apply
in the public domain

entries.intent: says on what basis the dataset is reached
entries.meaning: licensed, open or public domain; a free source fills the same record with open or public domain, no meters, and attribution
entries.not_meaning: a price, which the registry listing carries

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.timeliness

allowed.meaning: not stated
served in real time
served behind real time by delay_minutes, with its delay_label
served at the end of the day
history only

entries.intent: says how current the dataset is
entries.meaning: one timeliness per dataset: a vendor serving real-time and delayed data declares two datasets, whose licences and meters differ
entries.not_meaning: the dataset's cadence, or how its rows arrive

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.delay_minutes
entries.intent: says the vendor's delay
entries.meaning: the minutes the vendor serves the data behind real time
entries.not_meaning: the declared delay the staleness check reads, which the catalogue's declared_delay_ns gives

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.delay_label
entries.empty: empty for a dataset that is not delayed; a delayed dataset's terms carry one (W10.1)
entries.intent: gives the words shown beside every delayed value
entries.meaning: shown with every value on pages, in exports and in every MCP answer carrying the dataset's fields, such as Delayed 15 minutes (ruling 386)

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.underlying_source
entries.intent: names the licensing source behind the vendor, where one is
entries.meaning: the source whose terms the vendor passes on, as the vendor names it, so counts can be kept per source as well as per dataset (ruling 387); where the vendor serves an aggregate, whose aggregate it is, in words -- Pyth's aggregate of its publishers. A data plugin declares it in its catalogue's default terms, through the SDK's typed declaration from contract 28 as amended 2026-10-31 (ruling 896); the deployment's licence keeps it unless the deployment admin changes it (W10.1); shown on the Data sources page and answered by dashboard__list_datasets
entries.not_meaning: the vendor or the aggregator, which the catalogue names; the class of source, which DatasetDeclaration.price_source_class says

changes.what: amended 2026-10-31 (ruling 896): a data plugin declares it through the SDK's typed declaration, naming whose aggregate where the vendor serves one; the Data sources page shows it

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.meters

allowed.meaning: not stated
display: counts persons, or devices where display_terms says so
non-display: counts plugins, or categories where non_display says so
enterprise: a flat fee per deployment

entries.intent: says which meters apply
entries.meaning: any of display, non-display and enterprise, each with its terms beside it; read by core from v27, with no effect until the deployment's counts exist (v28)
entries.not_meaning: a price, which the registry listing carries; a count

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.display_terms
entries.empty: unset where the display meter does not apply
entries.intent: says how the display meter counts
entries.meaning: the unit, the population billed, and whether and how professionals are priced apart
entries.not_meaning: display itself, which the boolean display said before v27

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.non_display
entries.empty: unset where the non-display meter does not apply
entries.intent: says how the non-display meter counts
entries.meaning: the categories, how they count, and whether one person's own automated use is free
entries.not_meaning: a plugin's categories, which the deployment admin sets at entitlement

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.enterprise
entries.empty: unset where the enterprise meter does not apply
entries.intent: says what the enterprise meter replaces and how
entries.meaning: the meters it replaces, its form, its scope and whether counts are still owed

entries.name: meridian.v1.DisplayTerms.unit

allowed.meaning: not stated
each person counts
each device counts: distinct client sessions per person

entries.intent: says what the display meter counts
entries.meaning: persons or devices
entries.not_meaning: a service account, which is never a person

entries.name: meridian.v1.DisplayTerms.count_basis

allowed.meaning: not stated
the vendor bills on the persons served a field in the month
the vendor bills on the persons able to read it in the month

entries.intent: names the population the vendor bills on
entries.meaning: served or entitled; the deployment keeps both counts, and this says which the vendor bills (ruling 377)

entries.name: meridian.v1.DisplayTerms.professional_split
entries.empty: false: one price for every person
entries.intent: says whether professional and non-professional persons are priced apart
entries.meaning: true: separate professional and non-professional prices
entries.not_meaning: a person's status, which is their own answer

entries.name: meridian.v1.DisplayTerms.professional_definition

allowed.meaning: not stated
the platform's one text, on the CT Plan's use-based test
the vendor's own text, with a link

entries.intent: says which professional test applies where prices split
entries.meaning: the platform's standard text or the vendor's (ruling 379)

entries.name: meridian.v1.NonDisplayTerms.categories

allowed.meaning: not stated
a trading platform: matching or crossing
automated trading
internal use
use serving clients

entries.intent: names the non-display categories the terms price
entries.meaning: by name, never number, since the plans number them differently (ruling 380)
entries.not_meaning: a plugin's categories, which the deployment admin sets at entitlement, defaulting by role

entries.name: meridian.v1.NonDisplayTerms.counts

allowed.meaning: not stated
each plugin counts
one fee per category, whatever the number of plugins

entries.intent: says how the non-display meter counts
entries.meaning: per plugin or per category

entries.name: meridian.v1.NonDisplayTerms.personal_exempt
entries.intent: says whether one person's own automated use is free
entries.meaning: true: one natural person's own automated use is free
entries.not_meaning: a service account's use, which counts on the non-display meter

entries.name: meridian.v1.EnterpriseTerms.replaces

allowed.meaning: not stated
the display meter for professionals
the display meter for non-professionals
the non-display meter

entries.intent: says which meters the enterprise fee replaces
entries.meaning: any of the three; all three is unlimited use
entries.not_meaning: a meter of its own beside the three

entries.name: meridian.v1.EnterpriseTerms.form

allowed.meaning: not stated
a flat fee
a cap: the most the per-unit fees can sum to

entries.intent: says the enterprise fee's form
entries.meaning: flat or a cap

entries.name: meridian.v1.EnterpriseTerms.scope

allowed.meaning: not stated
the deployment

entries.intent: says what the enterprise fee covers
entries.meaning: the deployment, the one scope until a vendor needs a wider one (ruling 381)
entries.not_meaning: a firm or a legal entity

entries.name: meridian.v1.EnterpriseTerms.reporting_waived
entries.empty: false: counts are still owed to the vendor
entries.intent: says whether counts are still owed to the vendor under the enterprise fee
entries.meaning: true: counts are no longer owed; the deployment counts regardless

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.derived_use_terms

allowed.meaning: not stated: read the deprecated derived_use, false as internal_only and true as not_restricted
data derived from it is not restricted
data derived from it may be made and stays inside the deployment
data derived from it may be made, and distributing it needs the vendor's licence or approval of the product first

entries.empty: unspecified: the deprecated derived_use read in its place, false as internal_only, true as not_restricted
entries.intent: says whether data derived from the dataset may be made, and where it may go
entries.meaning: the terms' three answers (W10.1; ruling 180), on a new field so the boolean derived_use keeps its type for one release (ruling 479). Derived data is what the platform's standard terms define once: it cannot be reverse-engineered to recreate the data, nor serve as a reasonable facsimile of it
entries.not_meaning: display of the data itself; the inherited licence of a derived row, which is the most restrictive among its inputs

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.derived_multi_instrument_free
entries.intent: says whether outputs over many instruments are free of the derived-data restriction
entries.meaning: true: an output over many instruments, an index or a portfolio's value, is not restricted even where single-instrument derivations are; false: it is restricted as derived_use_terms says
entries.not_meaning: a single-instrument derivation, which derived_use_terms answers

entries.name: meridian.v1.DatasetLicence.derived_creation_is_non_display
entries.empty: false: deriving from it does not count on the non-display meter
entries.intent: says whether deriving from the dataset counts on the non-display meter
entries.meaning: true: a plugin deriving from the dataset counts on the non-display meter
entries.not_meaning: whether derived data may be made, which derived_use_terms says

allowed.meaning: not stated

entries.intent: bounds a page
entries.meaning: how many sync statuses a page holds at most
entries.not_meaning: a promise that a page is full

entries.name: meridian.v1.ListSyncStatusesRequest.cursor
entries.intent: asks for the next page
entries.meaning: opaque: the previous reply's next_cursor

entries.name: meridian.v1.ListSyncStatusesReply.statuses
entries.empty: empty when none was heard for an account in scope
entries.intent: answers the sync statuses recorded
entries.meaning: each as it was announced (W2.13): the latest per account, or, read since a watermark, every one after it in the order recorded
entries.not_meaning: a statement that a connection is healthy: an empty page says only that none was heard

entries.name: meridian.v1.ListSyncStatusesReply.next_cursor
entries.intent: points at the next page
entries.meaning: opaque, passed back as cursor

entries.name: meridian.v1.ListSyncStatusesReply.as_of
entries.intent: says the point in the street's record the page was read at
entries.meaning: what a reader passes as since

entries.name: meridian.v1.ExternalAccountsEvent.accounts
entries.empty: empty when the connection reaches none
entries.intent: lists every external account a connection reaches, as the plugin sees it now
entries.meaning: the whole list each time, published before anything is recorded against any of them, so linking one (W6.4) is a choice among those on offer; one missing from it is one the connection no longer reaches

entries.name: meridian.v1.ExternalAccount.external_account_id
entries.intent: identifies an external account, stably
entries.meaning: stable across the connection's reconnections, which the plugin makes so where its source does not; the external_account_id the account's rows name; a handle the source wants on each call stays inside the plugin

entries.name: meridian.v1.ExternalAccount.name
entries.empty: empty where the custodian gives none
entries.intent: names the external account as a person there would recognise it
entries.meaning: the custodian's own name for it

entries.name: meridian.v1.ExternalAccount.venue_account_type
entries.empty: empty where the custodian gives none, and from a plugin on v11
entries.intent: showed, until v11, the custodian's own word for the kind of account
entries.meaning: verbatim and for display only; accepted from a plugin before v11 for its notice, and shown only where no kind is sent
entries.not_meaning: what the account may do: nothing reads meaning into it

deprecated.why: the plugin converts the venue's type to the account kind, and sends it as reported only when it does not convert

entries.name: meridian.v1.ExternalAccount.account_kind

allowed.meaning: not known: the custodian's type says neither cash nor margin nor retirement; what a plugin sends when the type does not convert, with the type as reported beside it
trades settle in full from the account's own cash, with no borrowing
the account may borrow against its holdings under a margin agreement
a tax-advantaged retirement account, whether or not it allows limited margin

entries.empty: unspecified is not known, and then the custodian's type travels as reported
entries.intent: says the account's kind, in the platform's own words
entries.meaning: converted by the plugin from the custodian's own type; for display and for grouping accounts across plugins
entries.not_meaning: what the account may do, which is the platform's restriction set when it is ruled; nothing gates on the kind

entries.name: meridian.v1.ExternalAccount.account_kind_as_reported
entries.empty: unset whenever the kind is known: set only beside a kind not known
entries.intent: carries the custodian's type that did not convert to a kind
entries.meaning: for a person to map, and counted as evidence the kinds may need to grow
entries.not_meaning: a kind any reader may act on: nothing past the plugin interprets it
